tasks.short: Review autopsies, laboratory findings and investigation reports

steps.what: Analyze autopsies, laboratory findings and investigation reports to review cases

tasks.design: Retain integrated case assessment with the pathologist using {DOCS} and {OTHER}, the existing laboratory information system. Automated summaries are not assumed to replace examination of source findings or reconciliation of contradictory evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case interpretation depends on medical context and uncertain or incomplete observations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing laboratory records provide access to findings without a new analysis service.
tasks.still_hard: Reconcile pathology, investigation evidence and alternative explanations.
tasks.human_edge: Own clinical interpretation and identify missing evidence.
tasks.altitude: Integrate evidence while preserving uncertainty and traceability.

reach.task: Resolve discrepancies between findings and case history

evidence.claim: Clinical case integration retains full time here; no task-specific validated diagnostic automation is established by model knowledge.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the laboratory information system.
Laboratory personnel and investigators supply source findings; obtaining clarification and reading evidence remain in s1.
The baseline is clinical assessment, without invented duplicate transcription.
No new automation is installed, so no extra maintenance is incurred.
research_questions: Is there a separately measurable retrieval burden before clinical assessment?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Clinical evidence integration retains full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Confirm laboratory workload, capacity, service targets and outstanding operational issues
Aggregate laboratory queue counts and elapsed times against recorded service targets
Manage medical laboratories by resolving priorities, staffing constraints and service risks

tasks.design: Configure an operational workload view in {OTHER}, the laboratory information system, using {BI} only if native reporting cannot supply it. Retain clinical prioritisation, staffing decisions and team management with the pathologist; the view creates no automatic clinical urgency or quality classification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Managers repeatedly consolidate queues before discussing operating constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing laboratory records can support deterministic counts and elapsed-time calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Interpret incomplete capacity information and balance service risks.
tasks.human_edge: Make accountable operational choices with the laboratory team.

ambition.what: Review operating pressure before routine management meetings.

tasks.altitude: Spend consolidation time on resolving laboratory constraints.

reach.learn: Queue data definitions and exception handling

evidence.claim: Operational queue aggregation is deterministic when identifiers, timestamps, status and targets are captured; this design and its time assumptions are model knowledge.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the laboratory information system; use its native reports before creating a separate dashboard.

In s1 the pathologist checks and captures queue identifier, receipt timestamp, current status, assigned capacity, equipment availability and locally agreed service target; all checking and missing-field clarification are included in its 25 hours.
Laboratory supervisors supply queue and capacity corrections; three incremental other-role hours cover additional capture and reconciliation rather than assuming free clean data.
Missing or inconsistent fields return to manual queue review in s3, without automated clinical decisions or result release.
Five extra focal hours per 100 baseline hours cover report definitions and validation; existing automatic reports earn no new saving.
research_questions: Does a native workload report remove manual consolidation after capture and maintenance are counted?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85; gross 15 minus 5 focal upkeep gives central net 10. E1 range 0-8 allows existing reporting and incomplete capacity data; clinical management remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop or adopt diagnostic tests and instruments

steps.what: Develop or evaluate tests and instruments for improved diagnosis of diseases

tasks.design: Retain assay development, validation and adoption judgement with the pathologist using {OTHER}, the laboratory information system, and {DOCS}. This task produces a supported recommendation; routine instrument operation and subsequent clinical deployment remain separate work.
tasks.previous_blocker: A technically promising test still needs context-specific clinical and analytical validation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing laboratory instrumentation and records support validation work.
tasks.still_hard: Establish diagnostic utility, limitations and acceptable performance.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise misleading validation evidence and take responsibility for an adoption recommendation.
tasks.altitude: Own evidence quality for diagnostic development.

evidence.claim: Diagnostic development and adoption are retained as professional validation work; no clerical savings baseline is established.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the laboratory information system.
The baseline includes validation design, evidence assessment and recommendation; it excludes routine assay production.
No new automation service or corresponding maintenance is proposed.
research_questions: Which repeated validation calculations, if any, are not already provided by laboratory software?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Development and clinical validation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Educate physicians, students and laboratory professionals

steps.what: Educate physicians, students and laboratory personnel through explanation, demonstration and supervised practice

tasks.design: Retain instruction, demonstration and observation with the pathologist, using existing {DOCS} and {LMS} materials. Reusing a slide deck does not establish a saving in supervised clinical education.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learners need explanation adapted to mistakes and clinical context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning materials support preparation and reference.
tasks.still_hard: Judge understanding and correct unsafe interpretation or technique.
tasks.human_edge: Observe learners and adapt teaching in real time.
tasks.altitude: Protect the quality of clinical laboratory education.

evidence.claim: Supervised laboratory instruction retains full time in this design; a separate materials-production burden is not assumed.

assumptions: The baseline is teaching and supervised practice, not an invented lesson administration process.
Learner questions and demonstrated performance arise during s1; no structured competency flag is assumed.
Existing materials remain available without a new automated service or added maintenance.
research_questions: Is materials preparation a measurable repeated burden outside supervised instruction?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Demonstration, feedback and supervision remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use reliable operational data while retaining diagnosis, validation and education.
reach: Work with supervisors on queue data
role.ambitious_version: A pathologist who reviews operational pressure with less manual consolidation while retaining clinical and educational responsibility.
